**How to submit:** Write your answers in a document or on paper. Upload the file or a clear photo to the university e-learning platform. Due: **one week after lecture 12**.
No task needs AI.

A small studio will **sell** *Lantern Lane*, a calm game about a girl who
lights lamps in an old town. Five of its assets:

| asset | made by | licence or contract | a) owner | b) decision |
|---------|-------------|------------|-------|-------|
| the girl (sprite) | an employee of the studio | employment contract | | |
| a wind sound | an artist on a sound website | CC BY | | |
| the title music | a paid freelance composer | no written contract | | |
| a door photo | found by image search | unknown | | |
| an old folk song | composer died in 1890; the studio recorded it | none | | |

## Task 1 · The rights check

a) In column a) of the table, write who owns each asset.

b) In column b), write "use it", "use it with a credit", or the fix (ask,
replace or remove).

c) The wind sound is "Night Wind" by Omar Faris, from
sounds.example.org/night-wind, under CC BY 4.0. Write its credit line with
the four parts of TASL.

{{< answer-space lines=2 >}}

## Task 2 · Two problems

a) May the studio use a cat drawing under **CC BY-NC** on its store page?
Why?

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

b) A team member says: "Our logo is only 30 % different from the logo
of a famous coffee brand, so it is fine." Is this right? What do you
advise?
